correctness.rationale: Setting s=h² and clearing the strictly positive denominator gives V_s′(x)=−2x[3(x²+s)^4+(4s+1)(1−4x²)]/D_s(x). An independent sparse exact bivariate polynomial expansion and threshold factorization confirmed the identity. The polynomial Q_s(y) is strictly convex for y≥0, with global minimum at y0=((4s+1)/3)^(1/3)−s and value 9r^4(r²−1); the sign changes at s=1/2. Its exact factorization at equality has only the positive double root y=1/2. This proves complete critical-point multiplicities for all real h>0. Analytic Taylor expansion around (x,s)=(1/sqrt2,1/2) gives local derivative 2sqrt2 μ−9sqrt2 ξ²+ controlled errors; integration across the two roots and multiplication by h/pi yields the 3/2 contrast coefficient. The checker confirms only algebraic subclaims; continuum root counts and asymptotic remainders follow from the written inequalities.

final_claim: The sum of three equal Poisson kernels centered at −1,0,1 has exactly three maxima and two minima for 0<h<1/sqrt(2), stationary outer inflections at h=1/sqrt(2), and a unique central maximum above that height; the outer peak-to-valley contrast is (8 sqrt2/(9 pi))(1/2−h²)^(3/2)+O((1/2−h²)^2).
limitations: Three equal positive and equally spaced atoms only; does not classify unequal masses or nonsymmetric sites.
